connectivity.body: PeeringDB’s interconnection-facility or coverage-floor measure increased materially to 1,378. The broader recorded footprint includes 168 active U.S. internet exchange points with 2,805 combined reported members and 90 U.S. international submarine cable systems. The higher figure materially expands the measured network footprint, but these counts do not show bandwidth, redundancy, or capacity available in a specific data-center market.
connectivity.headline: Network coverage rises materially, without a matching measure of capacity

data_center.body: Available records list 1,556 sites in development, equal to about half of the 3,068 operating sites. A separate active-pipeline series tracks 894 sites. Data Center Dynamics reported that ServerDomes broke ground on a campus outside El Paso, providing a current example of development moving into construction. The aggregate inventory remains large, although one groundbreaking does not establish the conversion pace for the broader pipeline.
data_center.headline: Data-center development remains extensive, with 894 sites in the active pipeline

economic_impact.body: Aggregate outcomes shifted to a less favorable mix. Nonfarm-business productivity growth eased slightly to 2.1% and real output growth to 2.3%, while unit labor cost growth rose materially to 2.4%. The labor-share index remains 8.3% below 2020, despite a slight improvement in the latest reading. These economy-wide measures do not isolate AI’s contribution, but they show a moderation in measured productivity growth alongside stronger labor-cost growth.
economic_impact.headline: Productivity eases as unit labor cost growth rises

finance.body: Operating cash flow covers current capital spending by 1.23 times, so the aggregate measure still shows internal funding capacity for current spending. At the same time, borrower strain increased slightly to 30.2 and the debt-financing pulse edged up to 0.5. CNBC reported that ING was seeking buyers for $500 million of data-center loans. The report adds a specific example of data-center debt being offered to the market, but it does not establish a broad credit disruption.
finance.headline: Current capital spending remains internally covered as borrower strain rises

macro.body: The AI buildout remains substantial, and current spending is still internally covered. Available project records list 1,556 data-center sites in development, against 3,068 operating sites, while published capacity associated with large-load campus records totals 200,987 MW. Operating cash flow covers current capital spending by 1.23 times. Morningstar also reported that hyperscaler AI investment will outpace near-term earnings, sharpening the distinction between funding current spending and the timing of its earnings contribution. Most market measures improved modestly, with a larger move in the median return. The AI Equity Index rose slightly to 32.9 and the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns reached 58.3%, while the median return increased materially to 6.5%. Credit indicators moved less favorably: borrower strain edged up to 30.2 and the debt-financing pulse to 0.5. CNBC reported that ING was seeking buyers for $500 million of data-center loans. The report does not establish a systemwide problem, but it grounds financing concern in a specific loan-sale effort. Labor signals also show selective rather than broad expansion. Two tracked AI-linked channels now have positive employment growth, with semiconductor manufacturing strongest at 2.0%, while the weakest channel contracted 5.4%. Semiconductor and electronic-component output growth is 19.9%. That pairing identifies semiconductors as a clear pocket of expansion, not evidence of broad labor-market gains.
macro.headline: The AI buildout remains extensive as credit strain firms and job gains stay narrow

market.body: AI-linked market measures have turned higher, but the improvement is uneven in scale. The median one-year return rose materially to 6.5%, while the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns increased slightly to 58.3%. The AI Equity Index also edged up, to 32.9. Morningstar separately reported that hyperscaler AI investment will outpace near-term earnings. That report does not explain the measured improvement, but it shows that stronger market performance can coexist with concern that heavy investment is running ahead of near-term earnings.
market.headline: AI-linked equities turn modestly higher, led by the median return

power.body: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, versus 1.8% for total retail demand, while retail electricity prices are up 5.1%. Utility Dive reported that PSEG Power plans a 200 MW nuclear uprate as it considers data-center deals. The reported uprate gives a defined project and scale, although it remains planned. Across the broader pipeline horizon, net planned generation additions total 227.6 GW. The PSEG report ties one proposed project to potential data-center business; the aggregate demand and price figures do not isolate AI’s role.
power.headline: PSEG plans a nuclear uprate as commercial power demand outpaces the total

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: AI-linked market measures improved across several dimensions. The AI Equity Index increased materially to 37.3, the median one-year return rose to 9.4%, and the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns reached 60.3%. Average sector trading pressure also increased materially to 44.1. The improvement is therefore broader than a move in the index alone, although positive performance is not universal.

headline.text: AI-linked equities strengthen across index, breadth and median returns

body.text: Financing conditions are moving in different directions. Borrower strain increased slightly to 30.2, while lender strain decreased slightly to 19.3. Operating cash flow still covers current capital expenditure by 1.23 times, but that ratio slipped, and cash reserves fell to the equivalent of 0.85 years of current spending. Moody’s Ratings said private credit was holding firm despite the AI debt wave, while Bloomberg reported SoftBank-led Asian bond losses as an AI rout spread to credit. The reports reinforce the uneven picture but do not establish a broad credit disruption.

headline.text: Borrower strain rises as lender strain eases and funding buffers narrow

body.text: Available project records list 1,556 sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the 3,068 operating sites. A separate active-pipeline series tracks 894 sites. Recent reports show projects at multiple stages: Fluidstack began construction on a 99-acre Virginia campus, Fluor won the EPC contract for a $4 billion Kentucky campus, and Google announced a $17 billion campus in Wyoming. These are substantial project-level commitments, but they do not establish how quickly the wider inventory will become operational.

headline.text: New campus activity underscores the scale of an already large development pipeline

body.text: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, nearly twice the 1.8% increase in total retail demand, while retail electricity prices are up 5.1%. Reuters reported that SpaceX plans a $24 billion gas-power and data-center project in Texas, a current example of generation and computing infrastructure being proposed together. Net planned generation additions total 227.6 GW through the pipeline horizon. Both the reported project and the aggregate generation total remain plans rather than completed supply.

headline.text: Commercial electricity demand outpaces total growth as SpaceX plans a combined power and data-center project
AI-linked markets strengthen amid large new data-center commitments and narrower funding buffers

paragraphs.text: AI-linked market measures improved across several dimensions. The AI Equity Index rose materially to 37.3, the median one-year return reached 9.4%, and 60.3% of covered companies had positive one-year returns. Average sector trading pressure also increased materially to 44.1. The improvement spans index performance, the median, breadth and trading pressure rather than a single market measure.

That stronger market tone sits alongside a data-center pipeline that remains large. Available project records list 1,556 sites in development, equal to roughly half the 3,068 operating sites, while a separate active-pipeline series tracks 894. Recent reports show activity at several stages: Fluidstack began construction of a 99-acre Virginia campus, Fluor won the EPC contract for a $4 billion Kentucky campus, and Google announced a $17 billion Wyoming campus. These developments do not show how quickly the wider pipeline will become operational.

Funding remains internally covered at current spending levels, but buffers narrowed. Operating cash flow covers current capital expenditure by 1.23 times, while cash reserves equal 0.85 years of current spending; both measures decreased slightly. Borrower strain rose slightly to 30.2 even as lender strain eased to 19.3. Moody’s Ratings said private credit was holding firm despite the AI debt wave, while Bloomberg reported SoftBank-led Asian bond losses as the AI rout spread to credit. The mix points to uneven pressure rather than a uniform lender retreat.

The physical buildout is also arriving in a firm power-demand environment. Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, compared with 1.8% for total retail demand, and retail prices are up 5.1%. Reuters reported that SpaceX plans a $24 billion gas-power and data-center project in Texas. At the same time, an economy-wide AI return remains difficult to identify from aggregate outcomes: nonfarm-business productivity is growing 2.1%, but real hourly compensation is up only 0.6%. These measures do not isolate AI’s contribution, so they cannot by themselves connect current infrastructure investment to broad economic gains.

editorial_synthesis.instructions:
You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.
